'''Norman WC Powell''' (born May 25, 1993)<ref name=ucla_bio>{{cite news|title=Norman Powell Biography|work=UCLABruins.com|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=207913792|accessdate=April 25, 2014}}</ref> is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. After entering his senior year in 2014–15 as the Bruins' top returning player, he emerged as a team leader, and received first-team [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the [[Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball|Pacific-12]].  Prior to joining UCLA,  he was a two-time all-state high school player in California, and led his team to a state championship.

==Early years==
Powell was born in [[San Diego, California]], to Sharon and Norman Powell Sr.<ref name=ucla_bio/> He was introduced to basketball by his uncle, Raymond Edwards. Powell decided to attend high school at [[Lincoln High School (San Diego)|Lincoln High]], which had just been rebuilt and lost many athletes.<ref name=painter_0320104>{{cite news|last=Painter|first=Jill|title=UCLA’s Norman Powell a slam dunk in San Diego|date=March 20, 2014|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20140320/uclas-norman-powell-a-slam-dunk-in-san-diego|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6P6o9aMWK|archivedate=April 25, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> He helped rebuild their basketball program,<ref name=painter_0320104/> leading the team to consecutive [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) San Diego Section 2A championships in 2009 and 2010.  The team also captured the 2010 CIF Division II Boys' State Championship, with Powell scoring 24 [[point (basketball)|points]] in a 74–59 win over [[Saint Francis High School (Mountain View)|Mountain View St. Francis]].  He finished his junior season averaging 19.7 points, 4.9 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 2.7 [[steal (basketball)|steals]], and earned first-team all-state as well as Western League Most Valuable Player (MVP) honors.<ref name=ucla_bio/><ref name=maffei_01132014>{{cite news|last=Maffei|first=John|title=Lincoln's Powell enjoying ride at UCLA|date=January 13, 2014|newspaper=U-T San Diego|url=http://www.utsandiego.com/news/2014/Jan/13/alumni-report-powell/|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6P6uK7viY|archivedate=April 25, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref>

In his senior year, he was again first-team all-state and league MVP, and averaged 20.4 points, 3.8 rebounds, 2.4 steals. Lincoln was 32–2 and won the league title with a 12–0 record. They were ranked No. 3 in California and No. 15 nationally, but were defeated 74–69 by Summit in the state semifinals.<ref name=ucla_bio/> He finished his high school career winning the San Diego County All Star Game Dunk Contest.<ref>{{cite news|last=Angulo|first=Blair|title=In transition with Norman Powell|date=April 27, 2011|work=ESPN.com|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/5787/in-transition-with-norman-powell|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6PBrXWYKT|archivedate= April 29, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Powell was listed as the No. 15 shooting guard and the No. 52 player in the nation in 2011.<ref>[http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/102170/norman-powell Norman Powell Recruiting Profile]</ref> Powell chose to play [[college basketball]] for [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] over [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]], [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] and [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].<ref name=maffei_01132014/>

==College career==
In his first year at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), he was the only true freshman to play significant minutes in [[2011–12 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2011–12]], when he averaged 17.8 minutes and contributed 4.6 points and 2.2 rebounds in 33 games, joining Tyler Lamb and [[Lazeric Jones]] as the only Bruins to play in every game that season.<ref>{{cite book|title=2013–14 UCLA Bruins Men's Basketball Media Guide|page=60|publisher=UCLA Athletics|url=http://issuu.com/uclabruins/docs/full_guide_8ad1830246e372/60?e=1901135/5335034|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6P7B10zy5|archivedate=April 26, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> While he excelled as a driving guard in high school, his role transformed at UCLA, taking less than one-fourth of his shots around the rim and close to half from outside on [[three-point field goal|three-point attempts]].<ref name=wang_03102015>{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Jack|title=Norman Powell is thankful for his UCLA career, both the good and the bad|date=March 10, 2015|newspaper=Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20150310/norman-powell-is-thankful-for-his-ucla-career-both-the-good-and-the-bad|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6WxOtoVgL|archivedate=March 11, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref>

Powell averaged 6.1 points in 22.1 minutes in [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2012–13]], making nine starts while playing all 35 games.<ref name=ucla_bio/> He began the season as a starter, but was later moved to the bench. His minutes declined from an average of 28.4 in the first seven games to 19 the following 26 games. After replacing injured starter [[Jordan Adams]], Powell's minutes increased to 37 per game.<ref name=yoon_04022013/> He considered transferring to San Diego State after the season,<ref name=katje_03222014/> but decided to stay primarily because UCLA coach [[Ben Howland]] was fired.<ref name=yoon_04022013/> Powell credited Howland for his development on defense, but he stated that "there were a lot of things going on that weren’t fair for me" and "I definitely wanted to see a change."<ref name=wang_03102015/><ref>{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Jack|title=Norman Powell talks about decision to stay at UCLA|date=May 22, 2013|work=insidesocal.com|url=http://www.insidesocal.com/ucla/2013/05/22/norman-powell-talks-about-decision-to-stay-at-ucla/|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6WxQwpmK6|archivedate=March 11, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> The Bruins hired [[Steve Alford]] as their new coach.<ref name=yoon_04022013>{{cite news|last=Yoon|first=Peter|title=Norman Powell staying after Howland firing|date=April 2, 2013|work=ESPN.com|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/13723/norman-powell-staying-after-howland-firing|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6P6wy90vT|archivedate=April 25, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref>
